verdict.rationale: Microsoft Copilot is itself a built-in AI assistant. It documents task delegation inside Word, Excel, PowerPoint and Outlook, and adds agentic modes: Cowork for multi-step tasks that deliver completed to-dos, and Browse with Copilot, which clicks, types and navigates in Edge under user supervision. A hands-on report says Copilot in Word could only append text and could not create tables or search and replace, which limits depth but does not contradict delegation itself; another user praises cross-document fetching. Missing for 10: detailed docs on Cowork's multi-step delegation scope, consistent independent corroboration of task completion quality in Office apps.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can delegate tasks to a built-in AI assistant inside the product

citations.quote: Prompt Copilot with the task, add and upload notes, then refine in the chat—all with Copilot in Word.
With Cowork, Copilot can also help with bigger, multi-step tasks and deliver completed to-dos.
Browse with Copilot lets Copilot perform actions directly in your Microsoft Edge browser, such as clicking, typing, and navigating tabs.
Hand off repetitive work so you can focus on what matters.
the way it can fetch data from across documents in 365 is really good
